name: GPT-6 Astra
archDisplay: Proprietary frontier reasoning model (architecture and size undisclosed); 1.05M-token context, text+image in / text out, five selectable reasoning efforts (low → max)
note: OpenAI's first GPT-6-generation model, launched September 3, 2026 as `gpt-6-astra` after a month of staged safety disclosure: previewed August 1 through ten solved open mathematics problems, then confirmed on September 1 as the first model OpenAI has ever classified **Critical** for cybersecurity under its Preparedness Framework (it can find and weaponise zero-days in hardened targets without human direction). Rolling out first to enterprises in the Trusted Access Program, with API, Plus, Pro, Business and Enterprise access following; advanced offensive-cyber capability stays gated behind Daybreak Blue. $10/$50 per Mtok (cached input $1.00, cache writes $12.50; >272K-token prompts billed at 2x input / 1.5x output; Fast mode 2x at up to 2.5x speed), 1,050,000-token context, 128K max output, April 30 2026 knowledge cutoff. PROVENANCE CAVEATS — every recorded row is OpenAI-run at maximum effort, and OpenAI does not say whether standard users can select that effort. Two headline claims are deliberately NOT recorded here: the ARC-AGI-3 99.9% (run through a Responses-API harness that retains reasoning across turns and compacts context — OpenAI has itself shown those settings can triple ARC-AGI-3 scores without changing the model, so the number measures the agent system; the public ARC Prize leaderboard's best result is Claude Opus 5 at ~30.2%, and the viral 98.6%/99.9% figures were flagged as unverified by third-party coverage) and the FrontierMath Tier 4 98% saturation claim (no independent corroboration). Its DeepSWE lead is also narrower than the launch chart suggests: OpenAI's own chart omits Muse Spark 1.3, which reports 75.4% against Astra's 74.1%.

results.notes: Agents' Last Exam, GPT-6 Astra launch table (Computer Use section). Score component per corpus convention. New high in OpenAI's comparison, ahead of Claude Opus 5 (55.5) and GPT-5.6 Sol (53.6), while using ~65% fewer output tokens than Opus 5.
AutomationBench, GPT-6 Astra launch table (Professional section); best in row, well clear of Claude Fable 5.1 (31.4).
Terminal-Bench 4.0, GPT-6 Astra launch table (Coding section); leads Claude Fable 5.1 (55.8) and Opus 5 (52.3).
Terminal-Bench Science 0.1, GPT-6 Astra launch table (Academic section). OpenAI reports 64.6% against Claude Fable 5.1's 52.6% at ~31% lower estimated API cost.
FrontierCode v1.1 Main set, GPT-6 Astra launch table. Ahead of GPT-5.6 Sol (47.5) but a hair behind Claude Fable 5 (53.5) and Opus 5 (53.4) — an honest non-SOTA row.
FrontierCode v1.1 Extended set, GPT-6 Astra launch table; behind Claude Fable 5 (64.9).
GPQA Diamond, GPT-6 Astra launch table (Academic section); new high in OpenAI's comparison. At a lower-cost effort setting it still reports 94.9% vs Sol's best 94.6%.
ARC-AGI-1, GPT-6 Astra launch table (Abstract reasoning); ties Claude Fable 5's 98.5.
ARC-AGI-2, GPT-6 Astra launch table; best in row ahead of GPT-5.6 Sol (92.5) and Claude Opus 5 (90.4).
ScreenSpot-Pro (no tools), GPT-6 Astra launch table (Computer Use); vs GPT-5.6 Sol 76.9 and Claude Fable 5 87.3.
OpenAI MRCR v2 8-needle, 256K-512K band, GPT-6 Astra launch table — saturated, vs GPT-5.6 Sol 91.5.
OpenAI MRCR v2 8-needle, 512K-1M band, GPT-6 Astra launch table; vs GPT-5.6 Sol 73.8. Meta reports 98.1 for Muse Spark 1.3 on the same band.

ExploitBench, perfect score reported in OpenAI's 'Path to Astra' preparedness post — the result that, with expert-led browser and OS compromise assessments, put Astra over the Critical cybersecurity threshold. Measured with Daybreak Blue access, not the default production configuration; OpenAI itself flags public-set contamination and built a private June-August 2026 port in response.
SRE-Bench (binary reverse engineering), pass@1 in a single attempt; 99.2% within four attempts, vs GPT-5.6 Sol's 55.9 / 68.7.
BenchCAD Vision2Code 1,000-file subset with Python tools, geometric-overlap score; vs GPT-5.6 Sol 83.3 and a reported 84.3 for Claude Fable 5.1.

ARC-AGI-2 independent verification on the ARC Prize public leaderboard (semi-private set), within a point of OpenAI's self-reported 95.0 — unusually fast independent corroboration of a frontier claim.
